questions.q: What can rapid implementation spreadsheet templates generate in one coordinated upload?
options: Chart of accounts values and hierarchies, the accounting calendar, legal entities, a primary ledger, and business units
Only cross-validation rules
Only reference data sets
Only currency conversion rate types
questions.explain: RI spreadsheets can generate a broad set of enterprise structure pieces together, rather than requiring dozens of individual setup tasks.

options: A type of chart of accounts segment label
The ADF Desktop Integrator, an Excel add-in that connects spreadsheet data to Oracle Fusion
A conversion rate type
A legal entity registration number
questions.explain: ADFdi is the Excel-based tool that lets consultants enter and upload data from spreadsheets directly into Oracle Fusion.

questions.q: For what kind of company is rapid implementation generally the most appropriate approach?
options: Only companies using exclusively secondary ledgers
A complex multinational with many legal entities and extensive segment hierarchies
A company with relatively simple, single-chart-of-accounts, limited-entity requirements
Only companies with no legal entities at all
questions.explain: Rapid implementation suits simpler requirements; more complex multinational setups usually need the detailed, screen-by-screen configuration this course covered.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a consultant still do after a successful RI spreadsheet upload?
options: Delete the uploaded structure and start over by hand
Skip all further review since RI spreadsheets cannot contain errors
Nothing further; the upload is a finished, go-live-ready implementation
Manually verify segment labels, balancing-segment-value-to-legal-entity mapping, and review cross-validation rules
questions.explain: RI spreadsheet output is a head start, not a finished implementation, and still requires manual review of key configuration details.

questions.q: What is FBDI used for in the rapid implementation toolkit?
options: Running cross-validation rules automatically
Bulk, file-based data import, typically for larger data volumes
Assigning business functions to a business unit
Defining a ledger's accounting calendar manually
questions.explain: FBDI (File-Based Data Import) supports bulk data import, complementing ADFdi for larger data volumes.
